name: Kartu Kredit Danamon JCB Precious

memberLevels.name: Dana kelolaan Rp 50 juta or more
memberLevels.condition: total funds under management at Danamon in the previous month of Rp 50.000.000 or more

memberLevels.name: Dana kelolaan under Rp 50 juta
memberLevels.condition: total funds under management at Danamon in the previous month below Rp 50.000.000

welcomeBonus: From 1 March 2026: Rp 1.000.000 cashback after Rp 25.000.000 of transactions within 2 months of approval, plus registering at least one kind of bill payment.
notes: The rate follows total dana kelolaan at Danamon in the previous month: Rp 50.000.000 or more earns 3x D-Point per Rp 2.500, below it 2,5x. Both need the month's accumulated retail transactions to reach Rp 1.500.000, and the uplift then applies across the whole month, not only the spend above the floor.

The RIPLAY states the 3x and 2,5x multiples but never the figure they multiply. PinterPoin gives the regular earning as 1 D-Point per Rp 2.500, which is what the entry uses and what the card earns below the Rp 1.500.000 floor.

The uplift is capped at whichever is smaller: retail transactions of one times the card limit, including a temporary limit, or Rp 300.000.000 a month. The Rp 300.000.000 ceiling is in the entry; the card limit is read from the card's own terms when the entry is applied, so set the credit limit before relying on the estimate.

From 1 June 2026 Danamon stopped paying D-Point on utility bills, taxes, petrol stations and invoicing. That is the second terms period; cycles before it keep earning on those categories. The change is from PinterPoin, not from the RIPLAY, which predates it — and the exact scope is a reading: utilities, government and taxes, fuel and business invoicing by category, with MCC 5541 and 5542 excluded as well for petrol.
8.000 D-Point once a month at Rp 10.000.000 of accumulated transactions, with no multiples for spending more.

Earning excludes insurance payments, cash advance, money transfer, balance conversion, QRIS funded by this card, any transaction converted to an instalment together with the monthly instalment charges, and cancelled transactions. Insurance is matched by category; the rest are matched on the words an issuer usually puts on the statement line, so a differently worded description will be missed and overestimated.
The card requires total dana kelolaan of at least Rp 50.000.000 to be issued, so the lower level applies to a holder whose balance has since fallen rather than to a new applicant.
Not modelled: the 5% cashback up to Rp 100.000 a month on routine bill payments, which needs at least five retail transactions of Rp 100.000 or more, and airport lounge access. Neither pays D-Point.
The card limit runs from Rp 15.000.000 to Rp 1.000.000.000.

The terms come from Danamon's own RIPLAY, the 26 August 2025 version, which gives no start date, so the first period runs open until the 1 June 2026 change. Secondary reporting also describes a later clarification that walks some of these changes back; it could not be read here, so if it softened the June exclusions this entry takes away more than it should.
Rounding is per full increment of Rp 2.500, confirmed by the cardholder: the remainder of a purchase earns nothing, so Rp 6.000 earns 2 D-Point at the base rate, not 2,4.

Six partners take D-Point: GarudaMiles and Enrich at 15 a mile, KrisFlyer and Asia Miles at 20, JAL Mileage Bank at 32, and AirAsia rewards at 10 a point. At 1 D-Point per Rp 2.500 that is Rp 37.500, Rp 50.000, Rp 80.000 and Rp 25.000 a unit. JAL is much the worst of them and AirAsia much the best.

Miles are taken out in blocks of 500, given by the cardholder, and the 500 is counted in miles rather than in D-Point. A block is therefore 7.500 D-Point at GarudaMiles and Enrich, 10.000 at KrisFlyer and Asia Miles, 16.000 at JAL and 5.000 at AirAsia. The entry stores both figures and validation checks that they agree through the ratio.

JAL takes at least 32.000 D-Point, which is 1.000 miles, from Japan Airlines's own page. Danamon's promotion terms put the same 1.000-unit minimum on AirAsia, which is recorded too but rests on promotion wording rather than a product page. Whether the other four carry it is not settled; they are recorded with the 500 block alone, so a balance between 500 and 1.000 miles may be shown converting when the bank would refuse.

Every block divides whole, so no fraction of a unit is lost anywhere. An earlier version read the 500 as D-Point rather than miles, which made a GarudaMiles block 33,3 miles and cost a mile to rounding; that was wrong.

Conversion runs through dpoint.id rather than the card's own statement, and Danamon runs frequent bonus promotions on it — 15% on airline miles, 80% and 100% on AirAsia points have all run. None of them is modelled, so a conversion made during one is understated.
